note: Akkad shrinks to its core at Dudu's accession; the compiled map kept the whole Cliopatria -2200 shape (Upper Mesopotamia, Assyria, northern Syria) until the dynasty ended in -2154.

region.text: everything the Akkadian shape held outside Akkad and Kish (and the Lagash district the ledger keeps to -2164): Dudu's kingdom 'was likely limited to northern Babylonia around Akkad and Kish'

events.note: 2189 BCE: Dudu (2189-2168) holds a kingdom 'considerably reduced in size and ... likely limited to northern Babylonia around Akkad and Kish'; 'a few votive inscriptions and references to military campaigns are known, which were likely intended to preserve what remained of his kingdom'. The page names Urkesh in Upper Mesopotamia (Tish-atal) among the lands that 'declared their independence'. The compiled map kept the whole -2200 shape (Upper Mesopotamia, Assyria, northern Syria) until the dissolve of -2154; the Sumer cut of the dossier's own -2189 loss does not touch it. Land left to no state (the pages name no holder).
